paper.title_en: Measurement of <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Sn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>119</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Sb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>120</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Sn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>116</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Sb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>117</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction cross sections at energies of astrophysical relevance
paper.abstract_en: The cross sections of the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Sn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>119</mn></mmultiscripts><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>120</mn></msup><mtext>Sb</mtext></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Sn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>116</mn></mmultiscripts><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>117</mn></msup><mtext>Sb</mtext></mrow></math> reactions have been measured using the activation technique over the center-of-mass energy ranges of 2.43–7.06 and 2.43–4.92 MeV, respectively. The measured energy range substantially covers the Gamow window of 1.85–4.53 MeV corresponding to stellar temperatures of 2–3 GK. The present measurements extend the measured energy range of the cross section for the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Sn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>119</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mtext>,</mtext><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Sb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>120</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction and help to clarify the existing experimental discrepancies for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Sn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>116</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Sb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>117</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction when compared with previous measurements. The extracted cross sections and the resulting astrophysical S factors, corrected for electron screening effects, were compared with predictions from the talys and non-smoker statistical models. The <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Sn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>116</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Sb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>117</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> cross sections agree well with the talys predictions. For <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Sn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>119</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Sb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>120</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>, however, standard model combinations proved inadequate, necessitating a tailored parameter set to reproduce the data reasonably well. Utilizing these validated models, stellar reaction rates for both proton-capture reactions were calculated using talys and compared with the rates from the JINA REACLIB database.
